title: 31 vulnerabilities found in x402 crypto payment network, risking exposure of 99% of trades
summary: Thirty-one new vulnerabilities have been found at major service providers supporting "x402," an HTTP-based cryptocurrency payment standard, CryptoSlate reported. The study covered 15 companies accounting for 99% of all transactions and found that every provider violated payment verification and settlement rules.The vulnerabilities fell into four categories: unauthorized use, asset theft, denial of service, and gas fee abuse. Researchers also confirmed two cases of unauthorized use, described as "Free shopping," that exploited a gap allowing services to be provided before settlement was completed.Major providers including Coinbase and PayAI acknowledged the vulnerabilities and began remediation work. The researchers urged merchants not to rely only on pre-verification and instead provide services only after final settlement is confirmed or adopt explicit rollback logic.

title: BitMart, BitMEX closures seen as signal of shakeout among crypto exchanges
summary: A shakeout appears to be underway in the centralized crypto exchange sector after BitMart and BitMEX announced business shutdowns in quick succession, BeInCrypto reported. The outlet said BitMart began winding down operations on July 26, three days after BitMEX announced its withdrawal, and the number of exchanges shutting down in July rose to three including AscendEX. Industry watchers see the prolonged bear market, a decline in retail altcoin investors, shrinking futures trading volume, tighter regulation and high operating costs as factors driving closures among small and mid-sized exchanges. The market may later be reorganized around regulation-compliant exchanges and institutional capital, while raising concerns that power could become concentrated in a small number of venues. BeInCrypto added that the latest closures do not necessarily signal a market bottom, with macroeconomics, liquidity, regulation and investment demand still remaining key variables for the next upcycle.

title: Metaplanet CEO says Strategy's core Bitcoin-buying logic remains unchanged
summary: Metaplanet CEO Simon Gerovich said Strategy’s Bitcoin acquisition strategy has not changed in its fundamental structure or logic.Gerovich said that when a software company with a market capitalization of about $1 billion added $250 million worth of Bitcoin to its balance sheet in August 2020, most people saw it as a one-off event. When the stock later rose 10-fold, he said, it was praised as a visionary move, and when it later fell nearly 90%, it was dismissed as a failed experiment. Despite those repeated swings in market judgment, Gerovich said Strategy has continued increasing its Bitcoin holdings and now owns 843,775 BTC worth more than $50 billion.

title: Bitcoin governance seen as key variable in quantum-computing response
summary: German crypto asset manager DDA (Deutsche Digital Assets) said Bitcoin’s governance structure is one reason advances in quantum computing could pose a threat to the network. DDA said financial institutions such as JPMorgan could shift to quantum-resistant cryptography through board approval and budget execution alone, while Bitcoin would require consensus among participants worldwide. DDA added decentralized networks may adopt quantum-resistant cryptography more slowly than traditional financial institutions, and said this reflects not so much a weakness in Bitcoin as a need to take its governance process seriously.

title: BTC enters undervalued zone, but lacks capitulation and upside momentum
summary: Bitcoin has entered an undervalued zone, but the capitulation typically seen at cycle bottoms has yet to emerge, on-chain analyst Axel Adler Jr said on X.Adler said the MVRV Z-score, a metric used to assess oversold and overbought conditions, fell to 0.42, around four times lower than its historical average of 1.7, but remained above zero. BTC’s seven-day realized profit and loss turned positive from negative, indicating on-chain selling pressure has eased. He said the market has entered a stabilization phase while undervalued, but clear bottom signals and the demand needed to drive a fresh upswing are still lacking.

title: LDP lawmaker seeks to ease Japan’s 2x crypto leverage cap
summary: Seiji Kihara, a lawmaker from Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party, said Japan’s two-times leverage limit on cryptocurrency trading is overly restrictive and pledged to pursue regulatory easing, Nikkei reported. Speaking at a financial summit in Tokyo, Kihara said sufficient liquidity and a functioning price mechanism are essential for the healthy development of the crypto market, adding that deregulation is an unavoidable trend.Kihara currently leads the LDP’s Next-Generation AI and On-Chain Finance Project Team, which is pushing regulatory changes aimed at improving market liquidity and attracting more cryptocurrency capital to Japan, according to the report.
